statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 20% holds the lower edge of the watch band while Stress rises to 79% at the top of the high band.
recommendation: Tail remains at the watch floor because the overnight NQ path is two-sided inside a narrow band and the marginal new 30,934.75 high was not held, so the mapped state is WATCH rather than a block. Stress rises on a broadly weaker Asian session, a dollar at 17-month highs, long-end Treasury yields near 24-year peaks, a Gulf conflict premium in energy and the September payrolls release at 12:30Z. The flagged window stays narrow, spanning 12:30Z to 15:00Z around the release and the U.S. cash open.
headline: NQ holds a narrow overnight band as Asia weakens and the dollar firms into the September payrolls print
body: NQ futures trade 30,898.25 (+0.45%) inside an overnight range of 30,760.25-30,934.75. The high was extended marginally over the past hour but was not held, and price sits about 36 points below it in a band roughly 0.56% wide, so the structure remains two-sided rather than persistently directional. Cash NDX closed 30,501.56 (+0.31%) on October 1 with a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range against a 52-week high of 30,770.63, and VIX finished at 16.39. The macro backdrop is materially more stressed than the price path. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34% on Thursday, its highest since 2002 after the steepest quarterly rise in 32 years, before easing to 5.2512% in Asia, while the 2-year sits at 4.8039%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for September 30 shows 10-year 5.29% and 2-year 4.88%. The dollar index at 102.09 is the firmest since April 2025, with EUR/USD at 1.1235 after touching 1.1215 and USD/JPY at 158.13, and Reuters describes wild overnight swings in both bonds and currencies. Brent at 101.95 and WTI near 92.84 retain a conflict premium as the United States is reported to be sending additional troops and carriers to the Middle East and China has suspended oil product exports. Asia is broadly lower: the Nikkei 225 is down 0.7-0.9%, the Kospi about 1% weaker, and the Hang Seng roughly 2.5% lower on its return from Thursday's holiday, with mainland China closed for Golden Week through October 8. A firm NQ against that backdrop is cross-asset divergence rather than aligned momentum. Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter beat and raised guidance on October 1 supported semiconductors, with Nvidia up 1.09%, which informs directional conviction rather than mean-reversion failure. The September employment report lands at 12:30Z with consensus near 90k against a 35k-180k forecast range, unemployment seen at 4.1% and average hourly earnings near 0.2-0.3%. Absent observed persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements, event importance, forecast dispersion and elevated volatility are scored into Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The shared Finviz context file was not used this run: its latest publication is dated September 29 and marked partial, far outside the 90-minute freshness contract, so the assessment rests on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band apart from one orange hour at 06:00Z on October 1, when Tail touched 25% on a brief trend-up read. Tail then settled into a 20-24% range and has printed 20% for the last twelve hours. Stress climbed from 72% to a 79% peak as the long-end yield selloff intensified and held 78-79% overnight, while Confidence stayed at 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail at the watch floor through the remaining Asian and European hours while the narrow overnight band contains price, steps it to 21-22% into the pre-release hours as depth thins, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering the U.S. cash open and the delayed-second-leg window after the payrolls print. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, shallow pullbacks and a long-end yield break back above 5.34%, not on the release itself. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% around the release and decays through the afternoon. From 21:00Z the weekend futures halt means no live price path forms, so the remaining slots hold the watch floor with Stress and Confidence stepping down, and the next checkpoints are the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, ISM Services on October 5 and the FOMC minutes on October 7.
